svg.text: Maritime Search and Rescue (SAR) Coordination · As-Is · notional · DoDAF 2.02 Operational Viewpoint
Detect, locate and rescue persons in distress at sea, and deliver survivors to medical care ashore.
Search area around the distress datum
Fishing vessel in distress raises the alert: 406 MHz beacon to satellites, Mayday call to MCTS
Satellites locate the beacon; the ground station and Mission Control Centre (MCC) alert the JRCC
MCTS acknowledges the Mayday and relays it to the JRCC
Met and ocean service supplies wind, sea-state and drift data to plan the search area
JRCC tasks the SAR aircraft and the Coast Guard cutter (named On-Scene Coordinator); SITREPs return
At JRCC request, MCTS broadcasts a Mayday Relay; vessels of opportunity divert to assist
On-Scene Coordinator directs the helicopter and vessels of opportunity in the search area
Air unit drops survival equipment and hoists survivors; the cutter recovers the rest
Survivors are landed ashore or flown by helicopter and handed to EMS and the hospital
